items.summary: Landowners in Illinois and Kentucky challenged the Army Corps of Engineers' river management practices, alleging that dam construction and dike placement caused increased flooding on their properties constituting a taking of property under the Fifth Amendment. The trial court dismissed the case for lack of jurisdiction, finding the evidence did not establish that a new flooding pattern had emerged within the applicable statute of limitations period. The Federal Circuit affirmed, concluding the trial court's analysis of hydrographical data contained no clear error.

___
items.summary: Raymond Crider, a veteran with a service-connected PTSD rating, appealed the Board of Veterans' Appeals' denial of his claim for total disability rating based on individual unemployability for the period prior to his PTSD rating's increase to 100% in March 2021. The Federal Circuit dismissed the appeal, finding it lacked jurisdiction to review the application of a regulation to specific facts, as Crider's arguments concerned the Board's factual determinations regarding his employment capacity rather than the interpretation of the regulation itself.

items.summary: The executive order directs the executive branch to use the terms "Super Intelligence" and "SI" in place of "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" in official correspondence, public communications, websites, and policy documents. The order defines these terms as encompassing the same technologies covered by 15 U.S.C. § 9401(3). Within 60 days, the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology must propose legislative language to establish a federal definition of "Super Intelligence" and "SI" and recommend conforming amendments to existing statutes.
items.title: Inaugurating The Era Of Super Intelligence

items.opening_verbatim: Eliminating Disease-Carrying Pests And Restoring Enjoyment Of The Great Outdoors – The White House Skip to content Menu Search Search for: Scroll Left News Gallery Livestream Election Integrity SAVE America Trump Accounts Trump TV Contact N
items.summary: The executive order directs federal agencies to develop and implement a campaign to reduce invasive mosquito and tick populations by specific targets: a 90 percent reduction in invasive mosquitoes and a 50 percent reduction in ticks in the District of Columbia by 2028, using non-chemical methods including land management, natural predators, sterile insect techniques, and biotechnologies. The EPA is directed to develop a regulatory framework for advanced tick and mosquito control technologies within 60 days, and HHS is directed to pursue rapid diagnostics, prophylactics, and therapeutics for tick- and mosquito-borne diseases within 90 days.
items.title: Eliminating Disease-Carrying Pests And Restoring Enjoyment Of The Great Outdoors

items.summary: Deymon Edwards sued Oregon correctional officers under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 for denying him a decontamination shower after he was exposed to pepper spray in October 2022. The district court dismissed his claims as time-barred under Oregon's two-year statute of limitations, but the Ninth Circuit reversed, holding that Oregon tolling law required the statute to be tolled during Edwards's required prison grievance process. Edwards's January 2025 filing was timely because tolling ran from when he initiated his grievance in October 2022 until he exhausted his administrative remedies in January 2023.

items.summary: Air Force employees sued Jeremy Burton, a former Deputy Chief Information Officer, under the False Claims Act for allegedly coordinating with a defense contractor to direct government contracts in violation of federal acquisition regulations. items.summary: Kandace Edwards filed a class action challenging Randolph County's bail system, which required arrestees unable to pay a predetermined bail amount to remain in jail until a preliminary hearing occurring weeks after arrest. After Randolph County changed its bail policy during the litigation, the county moved to dismiss the case as moot; the district court granted the motion. The appellate court reversed the mootness dismissal, holding that a defendant's mid-litigation change in policy does not eliminate a class action, and allowed the class to proceed with challenges to the prior practices and as-applied challenges to the current system.
items.title: Kandace Edwards v. Randolph County Sheriff, et al

items.summary: The executive order directs the establishment of America.gov as a unified digital point of entry for Federal information and services, operated by the Administrator of General Services in coordination with the National Design Studio and the Office of Management and Budget. Covered services—public-facing Federal services serving more than 100,000 users annually and accessible online—must be integrated with America.gov using Login.gov as the authentication mechanism, while agency custody of records and existing access methods remain preserved. Agencies shall identify covered services and integrate them within parameters set by OMB, ensuring data minimization and secure authorization practices.
items.title: Streamlining Access to Government Services Through America.gov

items.summary: The Romance Scam Prevention Act requires online dating service providers to notify members within 24 hours (or up to three days in certain circumstances) when they have received messages from members whose accounts have been banned for fraud risk, including the username of the banned member, warnings about false identities, and information about fraud prevention best practices. The Federal Trade Commission enforces the law, and providers are granted liability protection for complying with these notification requirements.
items.title: HR 2481 ENR: Romance Scam Prevention Act

items.summary: The Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary Modification Act directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey approximately 7.43 acres of federal land within the park to Mississippi without payment for use in facilitating public access and enhancing visitor experience consistent with the park's interpretative mission. The park's boundary shall be modified to exclude the conveyed land, and the Secretary retains authority to impose use restrictions and ensure the land does not adversely impact park resources.
items.title: HR 4467 ENR: Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary Modification Act

items.opening_verbatim: I One Hundred Nineteenth Congress of the United States of America At the Second Session Begun and held at the City of Washington on Saturday, the third day of January, two thousand and twenty-six H. R. 952 AN ACT To convey the reversionary
items.summary: The Reversionary Interest Conveyance Act authorizes the Bureau of Land Management to convey reversionary interests of the United States in approximately 8.43 acres of federal land in Sacramento, California to current private owners at fair market value within two years of request. Proceeds from such sales shall be deposited in the Federal Land Disposal Account for use as authorized by the Federal Land Transaction Facilitation Act, with all conveyance costs paid by buyers.
items.title: HR 952 ENR: Reversionary Interest Conveyance Act

items.summary: The executive order directs the executive branch to use the terms "Super Intelligence" and "SI" in place of "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" in official correspondence, public communications, websites, and policy documents. The order defines these terms as encompassing the same technologies covered by 15 U.S.C. § 9401(3). Within 60 days, the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology must propose legislative language to establish a federal definition of "Super Intelligence" and "SI" and recommend conforming amendments to existing statutes.
items.title: Inaugurating The Era Of Super Intelligence

items.opening_verbatim: Eliminating Disease-Carrying Pests And Restoring Enjoyment Of The Great Outdoors – The White House Skip to content Menu Search Search for: Scroll Left News Gallery Livestream Election Integrity SAVE America Trump Accounts Trump TV Contact N
items.summary: The executive order directs federal agencies to develop and implement a campaign to reduce invasive mosquito and tick populations by specific targets: a 90 percent reduction in invasive mosquitoes and a 50 percent reduction in ticks in the District of Columbia by 2028, using non-chemical methods including land management, natural predators, sterile insect techniques, and biotechnologies. The EPA is directed to develop a regulatory framework for advanced tick and mosquito control technologies within 60 days, and HHS is directed to pursue rapid diagnostics, prophylactics, and therapeutics for tick- and mosquito-borne diseases within 90 days.
items.title: Eliminating Disease-Carrying Pests And Restoring Enjoyment Of The Great Outdoors

items.opening_verbatim: Streamlining Access to Government Services Through America.gov – The White House Skip to content Menu Search Search for: Scroll Left News Gallery Livestream Election Integrity SAVE America Trump Accounts Trump TV Contact News Contact Electi
items.summary: The executive order directs the establishment of America.gov as a unified digital point of entry for Federal information and services, operated by the Administrator of General Services in coordination with the National Design Studio and the Office of Management and Budget. Covered services—public-facing Federal services serving more than 100,000 users annually and accessible online—must be integrated with America.gov using Login.gov as the authentication mechanism, while agency custody of records and existing access methods remain preserved. Agencies shall identify covered services and integrate them within parameters set by OMB, ensuring data minimization and secure authorization practices.
items.title: Streamlining Access to Government Services Through America.gov
